title.narrative: (Theme 3) Bridging GBV Response Gaps in Five Contested Woredas of Conflict-Affected Northern Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project is a targeted GBV prevention and response initiative in contested woredas that are severely affected by protracted conflict, displacement, and recurrent drought, which have heightened vulnerabilities—especially for women, girls, persons with disabilities, and the elderly. Approximately 40% of health facilities in these conflict zones are non-functional, severely limiting access to essential health services, including GBV cases. The erosion of social support systems and destruction of infrastructure have intensified exposure to GBV, while limited humanitarian access continues to hinder effective response.ltbrgtThe project aims to enhance the protection and resilience of women and girls through a coordinated GBV response framework that integrates direct service delivery, community outreach, capacity building, and system strengthening. Key interventions include training for GBV service providers on case management, psychosocial support (PSS), Psychological First Aid (PFA), and Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) to ensure high-quality survivor care. Health facilities will be supported with contraceptive supplies and technical guidance to sustain essential reproductive health services.ltbrgtWGFS will be established or reinforced to provide safe environments offering counseling, legal referrals, and life skills programming. The project will operationalize GBV referral systems and coordinate GBV Area of Responsibility (AoR) mechanisms to improve local capacity and accountability. Dignity kits will be distributed for 1750 survivors of violence, and direct cash support will be provided to 675 GBV survivors and vulnerable women and girls to cover the costs related to case management. Provide mental health and psychosocial support services for 1350 survivors of violence and vulnerable and at risk women and girls, the project will also avail emergency contrastive and CMR supplies that can serve up to 1345 women and girls, 4000 IEC BCC materials will be prepared and utilized in community-level campaigns ltbrgtawareness raise of SRHR, and PSEA, promoting positive behavioral change. Besides, capacity building training will also be provided for frontline service providers. ltbrgtThe project will be implemented in Ofla, Chercher, Zata, Maitsebri, and Telemeti Woredas that are affected by conflict, high GBV incidence, displacement, and lack of accessible services. Both ActionAid Ethiopia(AAE) and New Millennium Women Empowerment Organization (NMWEO) have operational presence in these areas leveraging their relationship, structures and systems for a quality project outcome. ltbrgtActionAid and NMWEO, a local women-led NGO, co-designed this project. ActionAid will provide overall lead role. In addition, it will directly implement the project in Ofla, Chercher and Zata woredas. NMWEO will lead activities in Mai-Tsebri and Telemeti Woredas. Both organizations will partner closely with the Women and Children Affairs Offices (WCAO), local health offices, NGOs, CBOs, and humanitarian coordination structures, including the GBV AoR. Collaboration with community leaders, women’s groups, health professionals, and protection actors will ensure effective delivery and local ownership.ltbrgtBeneficiary Identification: Survivors and at-risk individuals will be identified via health facilities, WGFS, mobile outreach, and referrals from community-based structures. Safe and confidential self-referral options will also be available. Target groups include survivors of sexual violence, early marriage, and abduction displaced women returnees persons with disabilities elderly women and female-headed households. A survivor-centered, ethical, and rights-based approach will be upheld in all phases.ltbrgtThis project seeks to reduce GBV risks and strengthen services through combining training, direct support, health system reinforcement, and awareness efforts, it will restore safety and dignity for survivors and build community resilience in partnership with local actors.ltbrgtlt/pgt
